prompt: Write a pipeline that gets all services and filters to only those with a Status of 'Stopped'.
hints: Start with Get-Service, then pipe to Where-Object.
Use $_.Status inside the Where-Object script block.

validation.hintOnFail: Start with the Get-Service cmdlet.
Use the pipe operator | to pass objects to the next cmdlet.
Use Where-Object to filter the services.
Filter where $_.Status -eq 'Stopped'.

explanation: Get-Service retrieves all services. Where-Object filters the pipeline to only those objects where the Status property equals 'Stopped'.

prompt: Write a pipeline that gets all processes, sorts them by WorkingSet64 in descending order, and selects only the Name and WorkingSet64 properties of the first 3.
hints: Chain three cmdlets: Get-Process, Sort-Object, and Select-Object.
Sort-Object uses -Descending to reverse the order.
Select-Object uses -First to limit the number of results.

validation.hintOnFail: Start with Get-Process.
Pipe to Sort-Object to sort the results.
Sort by and select the WorkingSet64 property.
Use -Descending to sort from highest to lowest.
Pipe to Select-Object to pick properties.
Use -First 3 to return only the top 3 results.

solution: Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object Name, WorkingSet64 -First 3
explanation: This pipeline sorts processes by memory usage (WorkingSet64) in descending order, then selects only the Name and WorkingSet64 properties of the top 3.

prompt: Write a pipeline that groups all services by their Status property using Group-Object.
hints: Start with Get-Service and pipe to Group-Object.
Group-Object takes a property name as its argument.

validation.hintOnFail: Start with Get-Service.
Use the pipe operator |.
Use Group-Object to group items.
Group by the Status property.

explanation: Group-Object clusters the service objects by their Status property, showing you a count of how many services are Running, Stopped, etc.

prompt: Write a pipeline that uses Measure-Object to calculate the sum of the Length property for all files in the current directory (use Get-ChildItem).
hints: Get-ChildItem lists items in the current directory.
Pipe to Measure-Object with -Property Length and -Sum.

validation.hintOnFail: Use Get-ChildItem to list files.
Pipe to Measure-Object to perform calculations.
Use -Property to specify which property to measure.
Measure the Length property for file sizes.
Use -Sum to calculate the total.

explanation: This pipeline gets all items in the current directory and calculates the sum of their Length (file size) property using Measure-Object.

prompt: Write a pipeline that uses ForEach-Object to output the DisplayName of each service in uppercase.
hints: Start with Get-Service and pipe to ForEach-Object.
Use the .ToUpper() method to convert to uppercase.

validation.hintOnFail: Start with Get-Service.
Pipe to ForEach-Object to process each item.
Access the DisplayName property with $_.DisplayName.
Call .ToUpper() to convert the string to uppercase.

explanation: ForEach-Object processes each service object in the pipeline. $_.DisplayName accesses the display name, and .ToUpper() converts it to uppercase.
